newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Range-bound Belgian stocks eye U.S. data.
newsitem.headline: Range-bound Belgian stocks eye U.S. data.

text.p: Belgian shares ended with small gains on Monday, lacking inspiration with Wall Street closed for a holiday and with OLOs unable to provide support.

Dealers said attention was now focused on a fresh round of U.S. data is due this week, starting on Tuesday with July leading indicators, seen rising 0.2 percent, and the August NAPM index, forecast at 52.9 compared with 50.2 the previous month.
Recent U.S. data has tended to show a stronger trend, raising concerns of a possible U.S. interest rate rise.
The Bel-20 index .BFX closed 5.16 points or 0.30 percent higher at 1,719.47, near the top of the day's nine-point range.
Total Belgian share volume was modest at 1.1 billion francs.
The re-weighting of the Bel-20 index, effective from September 23, continued to cause portfolios to be shuffled and volatility in some of the stocks particularly affected.
One of these, insurer Royal Belge - whose weighting in the index is set to fall from 100 shares to 68 shares - leapt 4.2 percent to 5,900 francs after sinking 3.9 percent on Friday.
Oil major Petrofina and banking stock Kredietbank, both of which will get a heavier weighting, rose 10 francs to 9,610 and 9,680 respectively.

Shipper CMB slipped from the day's highs to close 1.0 percent or 25 francs higher at 2,460, after earlier touching 2,535. The stock was boosted by news late Friday CMB would pay an exceptional interim net dividend of 200 francs a share.
Also buoyed by good results at the end of last week was holding Gevaert, which rose 2.5 percent or 50 francs to 2,030.
